name: Microsoft Edge for Business
description: Basisset aan aanbevolen beveiligingsinstellingen voor Microsoft Edge for Business, gebaseerd op de Microsoft Edge Security Configuration Template (SCT) v151 als referentie.

settings.name: Allow autonomous (agentic) actions in Copilot Mode
settings.description: Controls whether Copilot Mode is allowed to take autonomous actions on a user's behalf, such as filling in forms or completing multi-step tasks on websites.
settings.rationale: Disabling agentic actions prevents an AI feature from autonomously interacting with sites and submitting data without explicit per-step user confirmation, reducing the risk of unintended or manipulated actions.

settings.name: Download Restrictions
settings.description: Restricts which files users are allowed to download based on Microsoft Defender SmartScreen's verdict for the file.
settings.rationale: Blocking downloads that SmartScreen flags as dangerous reduces the risk of malware reaching the endpoint via the browser.

settings.name: Enable unsafe SwiftShader fallback for WebGL
settings.description: Controls whether Edge is allowed to fall back to the unsafe (non-sandboxed) SwiftShader software GPU renderer for WebGL content.
settings.rationale: The unsafe SwiftShader path has known security weaknesses; disabling it removes an attack surface used in some sandbox-escape exploit chains.

settings.id: Internet Explorer Integration - Reload in IE mode
settings.name: Allow reload of a page in Internet Explorer mode
settings.description: Controls whether the 'Reload in Internet Explorer mode' option is available to end users from the page menu.
settings.rationale: Preventing users from manually forcing pages into the legacy, less-secure IE rendering engine reduces exposure to legacy engine vulnerabilities.

settings.name: Allow users to proceed past SSL/TLS certificate warnings
settings.description: Controls whether users can click through the browser's certificate error interstitial to continue to a site with an invalid certificate.
settings.rationale: Blocking the click-through option prevents users from bypassing certificate warnings, reducing exposure to TLS interception and man-in-the-middle attacks.

settings.name: Allow Microsoft Edge to use the Windows notification system
settings.description: Controls whether Edge is allowed to use the native Windows notification system to display web notifications.
settings.rationale: Using the native, OS-managed notification center keeps web notification behaviour consistent with Windows notification settings and auditing.

settings.id: Internet Explorer Integration - Zone Identifier for MHT files
settings.name: Allow IE mode to bypass the Mark-of-the-Web zone check for MHT/MHTML files
settings.description: Controls whether MHT/MHTML files are exempted from the zone identifier (Mark-of-the-Web) security check when opened in Internet Explorer mode.
settings.rationale: Keeping the zone check enforced ensures that MHT/MHTML files downloaded from the internet are still treated as untrusted content, preventing a known technique for smuggling malicious active content.

settings.name: Browser sign-in behavior
settings.description: Controls whether users can sign in to the browser with their work or school account.
settings.rationale: Enabling (rather than disabling or forcing) browser sign-in lets the organization manage profiles and sync settings via the signed-in account while still giving users a predictable sign-in flow.

settings.name: Prevent removal of the enterprise/managed browser profile
settings.description: Prevents end users from deleting the managed browser profile that is provisioned for the organization.
settings.rationale: Preventing profile deletion ensures that policy, bookmarks, extensions and security controls tied to the managed profile cannot be removed by the end user.

settings.name: Preferred cipher suite compliance mode for SSH connections
settings.description: Restricts the SSH symmetric cipher suites negotiated by Edge (e.g. for the built-in terminal/DevTools SSH usage) to the Commercial National Security Algorithm (CNSA) suite.
settings.rationale: Enforcing CNSA-approved ciphers aligns cryptographic negotiation with national security algorithm guidance and removes weaker legacy ciphers from the negotiation set.

settings.id: Cryptography Compliance - Prefer Slow Key Exchange Algorithms (SSH)
settings.name: Preferred key exchange algorithm compliance mode for SSH connections
settings.description: Restricts the SSH key exchange algorithms negotiated by Edge to the CNSA 2.0 (post-quantum ready) algorithm set.
settings.rationale: Enforcing CNSA 2.0 key exchange algorithms moves key agreement toward quantum-resistant algorithms and removes weaker legacy key exchange methods.

settings.name: Default search provider name
settings.description: Sets the display name of the default search provider used by the address bar and search box.
settings.rationale: Standardizing the default search provider name keeps the search experience consistent and predictable across managed devices.

settings.name: Default search provider search URL
settings.description: Sets the URL template used to perform a search with the default search provider.
settings.rationale: Centrally configuring the search URL prevents the default search engine from being silently changed by extensions or local user settings.

settings.name: Default search provider suggestion URL
settings.description: Sets the URL template used to retrieve search suggestions as the user types in the address bar.
settings.rationale: Pinning the suggestion URL to the approved provider keeps autocomplete/suggestion traffic going to a known, organization-approved endpoint.

settings.name: Enable the default search provider
settings.description: Enables use of the organization-configured default search provider.
settings.rationale: This must be enabled for the configured default search provider name/URLs above to take effect.

settings.name: Enable DNS interception checks
settings.description: Enables checks that detect when a network is intercepting DNS requests (e.g. redirecting all lookups to a single page), which otherwise disables certain navigation-correction features.
settings.rationale: Keeping interception checks enabled helps Edge correctly detect captive portals and DNS hijacking conditions rather than silently trusting intercepted responses.

settings.name: Warn when downloading files from insecure (HTTP) sources
settings.description: Shows a warning when a user downloads a file over an insecure, non-HTTPS connection.
settings.rationale: Warning on insecure downloads helps users recognize when a file may have been tampered with in transit due to the lack of transport encryption.

settings.name: Block loading of dynamic/unsigned code into the browser process
settings.description: Configures the Arbitrary Code Guard (ACG) mitigation that blocks the browser process from loading dynamically generated or unsigned code, and whether users can opt out.
settings.rationale: Blocking dynamic code injection into the browser process closes off a common post-exploitation technique used to escalate from a compromised renderer to the privileged browser process.

settings.name: Enable typosquatting detection
settings.description: Warns users when they navigate to a URL that closely resembles a popular domain (a common typosquatting pattern).
settings.rationale: Typosquatting warnings help protect users from phishing and credential-harvesting sites that rely on domain-name look-alikes.

settings.name: Enable Microsoft Edge Workspaces
settings.description: Controls whether the Edge Workspaces feature (shared, synced tab groups) is available to users.
settings.rationale: Enabling Workspaces supports approved collaborative browsing scenarios under the organization's managed-profile and DLP controls.

settings.name: Enable application-bound encryption for locally stored secrets
settings.description: Enables application-bound encryption, which ties encryption of locally stored secrets (such as cookies and saved passwords) to the Edge application itself rather than only the user's Windows profile.
settings.rationale: Application-bound encryption raises the bar against malware that attempts to read browser-stored secrets directly from disk outside of the browser process.

settings.id: Browser Legacy Extension Points Blocking Enabled
settings.name: Block legacy extension points
settings.description: Blocks third-party software from using legacy Windows extension points (e.g. certain injected DLLs/hooks) to interact with the browser process.
settings.rationale: Blocking legacy extension points reduces the attack surface exposed to third-party code injection, including some classes of adware and malware.

settings.name: Enable process isolation (site isolation)
settings.description: Enables Edge's site isolation security architecture, which renders cross-site content in separate OS processes.
settings.rationale: Process/site isolation limits the blast radius of a compromised renderer process, making it significantly harder for a malicious site to read data belonging to another site.

settings.name: Enable App Container sandboxing for the renderer process
settings.description: Runs the browser's renderer processes inside a Windows AppContainer sandbox.
settings.rationale: AppContainer sandboxing further restricts what a compromised renderer process can access on the underlying operating system.

settings.name: Enforce strict site isolation for all sites
settings.description: Forces every site to be rendered in its own dedicated process, regardless of Edge's default site-isolation heuristics.
settings.rationale: Strict, non-heuristic site isolation closes gaps where Edge might otherwise co-locate sites in the same process, further strengthening defense against side-channel and cross-site data leaks.

settings.id: WebRTC Respect OS Routing Table Enabled
settings.name: Make WebRTC respect the OS routing table
settings.description: Forces WebRTC to use the network interface selected by the operating system's routing table instead of enumerating all available interfaces.
settings.rationale: Restricting WebRTC's interface enumeration reduces the amount of local network topology information that can be leaked to a remote site.

settings.name: Enable the network service sandbox
settings.description: Runs the browser's network service in its own sandboxed process rather than inside a less-restricted process.
settings.rationale: Sandboxing the network service limits what an attacker can do if that service is compromised, consistent with Edge/Chromium's process-sandboxing security model.

settings.name: Enhance your Security (Edge hardware-enforced security modes)
settings.description: Enables Microsoft Edge's built-in 'Enhance security' feature, which applies additional exploit mitigations (such as stricter memory and JIT protections) to the browser, at either Balanced or Strict level.
settings.rationale: The Balanced mode applies the strongest practical mitigations against memory-safety exploits for the sites users actually need, while keeping compatibility acceptable for day-to-day browsing.

settings.name: Block installation of extensions from outside the approved store flow
settings.description: Blocks extensions from being silently installed into Edge by other locally installed applications (so-called 'external' extension installs).
settings.rationale: Blocking external/silent extension installation prevents other software on the device from adding browser extensions without the user's or IT's awareness.

settings.name: Extension install blocklist
settings.description: Defines the set of extensions that are blocked from installation. A value of '*' blocks all extensions unless explicitly allow-listed via the extension install allowlist.
settings.rationale: Blocking all extensions by default and only allow-listing approved ones enforces a deny-by-default posture for browser extensions, which are a common vector for data exfiltration and credential theft.

settings.name: Force users to sign in and sync their browser profile
settings.description: Forces browser sync to be enabled for users who sign in with their work or school account, so that managed settings and data sync to their profile.
settings.rationale: Forcing sync ensures that managed bookmarks, favorites, extensions and settings are consistently applied and backed up across a user's managed devices.

settings.name: Allow use of local, on-device generative AI foundational models
settings.description: Controls whether Edge is permitted to download and run local, on-device generative AI foundation models for AI-powered features.
settings.rationale: Disabling local foundation models prevents AI features from running unreviewed, on-device models and processing organizational data outside of approved, centrally governed AI services.

settings.name: Hide the first-run / welcome experience
settings.description: Suppresses the first-run welcome screens, import wizard and related onboarding prompts shown the first time Edge starts.
settings.rationale: Hiding the first-run experience provides a clean, consistent first launch for managed devices and avoids users being prompted to import data from other browsers or sign in before policy is applied.

settings.id: HTTP Authentication - Basic Auth Over HTTP Enabled
settings.name: Allow HTTP Basic authentication over unencrypted HTTP
settings.description: Controls whether Edge allows Basic authentication challenges to be completed over a plain, unencrypted HTTP connection.
settings.rationale: Disabling Basic auth over HTTP prevents credentials from being transmitted in a form that is trivially intercepted on the network.

settings.name: Supported HTTP authentication schemes
settings.description: Restricts integrated HTTP authentication to the specified schemes.
settings.rationale: Limiting authentication to NTLM and Negotiate (Kerberos) removes weaker or legacy authentication schemes (such as Digest or Basic) from being offered during integrated authentication.

settings.id: Identity - M365 Auth Popups in Work Profile Enabled
settings.name: Allow Microsoft 365 authentication pop-ups in the work profile
settings.description: Allows Microsoft 365 sign-in pop-up windows to be associated with and opened in the user's managed work profile.
settings.rationale: Keeping Microsoft 365 authentication pop-ups scoped to the work profile avoids credentials and session tokens leaking into an unmanaged personal profile.

settings.name: Enable proactive authentication workflow
settings.description: Enables Edge's proactive sign-in workflow, which detects when a user is browsing unauthenticated to a work-related site and prompts them to sign in with their work account.
settings.rationale: Proactively prompting for the correct identity reduces the chance that work data is accessed from, or saved into, an unmanaged or incorrect browser profile.

settings.name: Actions to perform when the browser idle timeout is reached
settings.description: Defines which cleanup actions (such as clearing saved sign-in data, browsing history or closing tabs) are performed automatically after the browser idle timeout policy triggers.
settings.rationale: Automatically clearing saved sign-in data after a period of inactivity reduces the window of opportunity for someone with physical access to an unattended, signed-in device. Corrected from the raw export, which captured this value as the truncated/malformed "'clear_password_signing" (leading apostrophe, missing trailing '_data'); confirm the companion IdleTimeout (minutes) policy is also configured before promoting this to production.

settings.name: Behavior for single-word intranet hostname navigation
settings.value: Disable the DNS interception checks and the intranet redirect (value index 2)
settings.description: Controls how Edge handles navigation to single-word hostnames that could either be an intranet site or a DNS-provider redirect/search result.
settings.rationale: Restricting automatic single-word intranet redirects reduces the risk of a user being silently redirected to an unintended or spoofed internal-looking destination. Validate the exact enum meaning for this value against current Microsoft Edge policy documentation before relying on it for compliance evidence.

settings.id: Manageability - MAM with Device DLP Enabled
settings.name: Enable Mobile Application Management (MAM) with device-based DLP
settings.description: Enables Edge to enforce Mobile Application Management data-loss-prevention policies in combination with device-based conditional access signals.
settings.rationale: Combining MAM and device DLP lets the organization enforce copy/paste, save-as and sharing restrictions for corporate data inside the browser, aligned with Intune app protection policies.

settings.name: Enable centralized Edge management features
settings.description: Enables Edge's management/manageability features used for centralized policy enforcement and reporting.
settings.rationale: Keeping centralized manageability enabled ensures Edge remains fully controllable and auditable through Intune/Microsoft Endpoint Manager.

settings.name: Allow user-level (non-admin installed) native messaging hosts
settings.description: Controls whether extensions can communicate with native messaging host applications that were registered at the user level rather than installed by an administrator.
settings.rationale: Disabling user-level native messaging hosts prevents an extension (or malware masquerading as one) from registering an unreviewed native application for the browser to launch and exchange data with.

settings.name: Enable Happy Eyeballs v3 connection racing
settings.description: Enables the updated Happy Eyeballs v3 algorithm, which races IPv4/IPv6 and multiple resolved addresses to improve connection reliability and speed.
settings.rationale: This is a reliability/performance setting; enabling the current algorithm keeps connection establishment behavior aligned with the supported, actively maintained implementation.

settings.name: Allow Password Monitor (breached-password detection)
settings.description: Allows the built-in Password Monitor feature to check saved passwords against known data-breach lists and warn the user if a match is found.
settings.rationale: Allowing breach monitoring helps users discover and rotate credentials that have been exposed in third-party data breaches.

settings.name: Enable the built-in password generator
settings.description: Enables Edge's built-in strong password generator, offered to users when creating accounts or changing passwords on websites.
settings.rationale: Offering a strong password generator encourages the use of long, unique, high-entropy passwords instead of weak or reused ones.

settings.id: Password Manager - Password Protection Warning Trigger
settings.name: Password reuse warning trigger
settings.description: Controls when Edge warns a user that they have reused a saved or corporate password on a site, e.g. only on password reuse events.
settings.rationale: Warning on password reuse helps prevent a single compromised credential from providing access to multiple accounts, including corporate sign-in pages.

settings.name: Primary (device) password requirement for the password manager
settings.value: Users may choose whether to set a primary password (value index 0)
settings.description: Controls whether users are required, allowed, or prevented from setting an additional primary password that must be entered before saved passwords can be viewed or used.
settings.rationale: This policy is configured but currently left at the permissive end of the range; validate against your organization's requirements whether a mandatory primary password should instead be enforced before this baseline is promoted to production.

settings.name: Allow exporting saved passwords
settings.description: Controls whether users are allowed to export their saved passwords from the Edge password manager to a file.
settings.rationale: Disabling password export prevents saved corporate credentials from being extracted to an unencrypted file that could be lost, synced to an unmanaged location, or exfiltrated.

settings.name: Enable passkey support in the password manager
settings.description: Enables support for creating and using FIDO2/WebAuthn passkeys stored in the Edge password manager.
settings.rationale: Enabling passkeys supports the organization's move toward phishing-resistant, passwordless authentication.

settings.name: Enable the built-in password manager
settings.description: Enables Edge's built-in password manager, allowing users to save and auto-fill credentials.
settings.rationale: Keeping the password manager enabled, combined with the other password-manager hardening settings in this baseline, gives users a safer alternative to reusing or writing down passwords.

settings.name: Enable RAM-based resource controls
settings.description: Enables Edge's resource controls that manage memory usage across tabs and processes based on available system RAM.
settings.rationale: This is a performance/stability setting; enabling it helps keep the browser responsive on managed endpoints with constrained memory.

settings.name: Enable Low Privilege App Container (LPAC) sandbox for printing
settings.description: Runs the Windows printing subsystem used by Edge inside a Low Privilege AppContainer sandbox.
settings.rationale: Sandboxing the printing pipeline reduces the impact of vulnerabilities in print spooler/driver code reachable from the browser.

settings.name: Use the operating system's native print dialog
settings.description: Forces Edge to use the native Windows print dialog instead of its own built-in print preview UI.
settings.rationale: Using the OS-native print dialog keeps print behavior (including driver-level security controls such as watermarking or restricted printers) consistent with the rest of the Windows environment.

settings.id: Printing - Print Preview Uses System Default Printer
settings.name: Default the print preview dialog to the system default printer
settings.description: Makes the print preview dialog default to the Windows system default printer rather than the last used printer.
settings.rationale: This aligns print defaults with centrally managed printer policy rather than caching a potentially unmanaged or unintended device.

settings.id: Profile - Show Profile Type in Profile Button
settings.name: Show the profile type (e.g. 'Work') on the profile button
settings.description: Displays a label on the profile button indicating the profile type (for example, Work or Personal).
settings.rationale: Clearly labelling the active profile type helps users avoid accidentally saving corporate data into a personal profile or vice versa.

settings.name: Availability of the Edge Remix (AI image) feature
settings.description: Controls whether the AI-powered Remix feature (image generation/editing) is available to users.
settings.rationale: Disabling the Remix feature prevents organizational or user image data from being processed by this generative-AI feature outside of approved AI tooling.

settings.name: WebRTC local IP address handling
settings.description: Restricts WebRTC to only use the default public network interface when gathering ICE candidates, rather than exposing all local interface IP addresses.
settings.rationale: Restricting WebRTC IP handling prevents websites from using WebRTC to enumerate local/private network addresses, a known technique for bypassing VPNs or fingerprinting internal networks.

settings.id: Scareware Blocker - Send Detected Sites to SmartScreen
settings.name: Send scareware-blocker detections to SmartScreen
settings.description: Allows information about sites detected by the local scareware blocker (fake virus-warning/tech-support scam pages) to be sent to Microsoft Defender SmartScreen for broader protection.
settings.rationale: Sharing detections with SmartScreen improves the overall detection of scareware/tech-support scam pages across the Edge user base.

settings.id: Internet Explorer Mode Toolbar Button Enabled
settings.name: Show the Internet Explorer mode toolbar button
settings.description: Controls whether a toolbar button is shown that lets users manually switch the current page into Internet Explorer mode.
settings.rationale: Hiding the manual IE-mode toolbar button prevents users from opting arbitrary sites into the legacy rendering engine outside of the centrally managed IE-mode site list.

settings.name: Enable Microsoft Defender SmartScreen
settings.description: Enables Microsoft Defender SmartScreen, which checks visited sites and downloaded files against Microsoft's reputation and phishing/malware intelligence.
settings.rationale: SmartScreen is a core anti-phishing and anti-malware control for the browser and should remain enabled on all managed devices.

settings.name: Block potentially unwanted applications (PUA) with SmartScreen
settings.description: Enables SmartScreen's detection and blocking of potentially unwanted applications (adware, bundleware, etc.).
settings.rationale: Blocking PUAs at download time reduces the volume of low-severity but disruptive unwanted software reaching endpoints.

settings.name: Allow SmartScreen to perform DNS-based reputation requests
settings.description: Allows SmartScreen to use DNS-based lookups as part of evaluating site reputation.
settings.rationale: Keeping this enabled ensures SmartScreen has the full set of signals available to evaluate site reputation accurately.

settings.name: Apply SmartScreen checks to downloads from trusted sources
settings.description: Ensures SmartScreen still evaluates files downloaded from sources that would otherwise be treated as trusted.
settings.rationale: Not exempting 'trusted' sources from SmartScreen scanning closes a gap that could otherwise be abused via compromised trusted sites or supply-chain attacks.

settings.name: Prevent users from bypassing SmartScreen site warnings
settings.description: Removes the 'Continue (not recommended)' option from SmartScreen site warnings, so users cannot click through to a flagged site.
settings.rationale: Removing the click-through option ensures SmartScreen warnings for malicious or phishing sites are enforced rather than advisory only.

settings.id: SmartScreen - Prevent Prompt Override for Files
settings.name: Prevent users from bypassing SmartScreen download warnings
settings.description: Removes the option to click through a SmartScreen warning and keep a file that has been flagged as malicious or unverified.
settings.rationale: Removing the click-through option for files ensures SmartScreen file warnings are enforced rather than advisory only, consistent with the equivalent site-warning control.

settings.name: Allow unrestricted access to SharedArrayBuffer
settings.description: Controls whether web pages can use SharedArrayBuffer without the cross-origin isolation requirements normally enforced by the browser.
settings.rationale: Keeping the cross-origin isolation requirement enforced mitigates speculative-execution side-channel attacks (such as Spectre) that rely on high-resolution timers exposed via SharedArrayBuffer.

settings.name: Pages to load on startup
settings.value: Open a specific set of pages (value index 4)
settings.description: Controls what Edge opens when it starts: the new tab page, the last session, or a specific, administrator-defined list of URLs.
settings.rationale: Opening a specific, administrator-defined set of pages at startup (configured below in 'Startup URLs') gives users a consistent, predictable starting point, such as the corporate intranet or portal.

settings.name: New tab page URL
settings.description: Sets the URL that is loaded when a user opens a new tab.
settings.rationale: Standardizing the new-tab-page URL ensures all managed devices default to the organization-approved landing page.

settings.id: Startup - Homepage is New Tab Page
settings.name: Use the new tab page as the homepage
settings.description: Configures the home button and home shortcut to open the configured new tab page rather than a separately configured homepage URL.
settings.rationale: Keeping the homepage aligned with the managed new-tab-page URL avoids a separate, potentially inconsistent homepage configuration.

settings.name: Show the Home button on the toolbar
settings.description: Shows the Home button on the browser toolbar.
settings.rationale: Showing the Home button gives users an easy, one-click way back to the organization-approved landing page.

settings.name: Startup URLs
settings.description: The list of URLs that are opened automatically when Edge starts, used together with the 'Open a specific set of pages' startup option.
settings.rationale: Opening the corporate Viva Engage feed at startup is an organizational choice to drive adoption of internal communications tooling; review and adjust this list for your own tenant before publishing.

settings.name: Use Edge's built-in (async) DNS client
settings.description: Controls whether Edge uses its own built-in DNS resolver instead of relying on the operating system's DNS resolution.
settings.rationale: Disabling the built-in DNS client forces Edge to use the Windows-managed DNS resolver, keeping DNS resolution consistent with OS-level DNS security controls (such as DNS-over-HTTPS policy, split-horizon DNS, or endpoint DNS filtering).

settings.name: Enable post-quantum key agreement for WebRTC
settings.description: Enables the use of a post-quantum-resistant key agreement algorithm when establishing WebRTC's encrypted media/data connections.
settings.rationale: Enabling post-quantum key agreement for WebRTC helps protect real-time communications against future decryption by quantum-capable adversaries ('harvest now, decrypt later').

settings.id: Recommended - Allow Extensions From Other Stores (default state)
settings.name: Recommended default: allow extensions from stores other than the Microsoft/Chrome Web Store
settings.description: Sets the recommended default state for allowing installation of extensions from third-party extension stores; unlike an enforced policy, users may still override this.
settings.rationale: This is configured as a recommended default rather than an enforced control; for a hardened production baseline, consider whether this should instead be enforced (Disabled) rather than left user-overridable.

settings.id: Recommended - Windows Hello for HTTP Authentication
settings.name: Recommended default: enable Windows Hello for HTTP authentication
settings.description: Sets the recommended default for allowing Windows Hello to be used to satisfy HTTP authentication challenges.
settings.rationale: Recommending Windows Hello for HTTP authentication encourages the use of stronger, phishing-resistant local authentication over typed passwords where supported.

settings.id: Recommended - Open External Links With Primary Work Profile
settings.name: Recommended default: open external links using the primary work profile
settings.description: Sets the recommended default for routing links opened from other applications into the user's primary work browser profile.
settings.rationale: Defaulting external links to the work profile reduces the chance that corporate links are opened in, or data is captured by, an unmanaged personal profile.

settings.name: Recommended default: Efficiency Mode level
settings.description: Sets the recommended default level for Edge's Efficiency Mode, which reduces CPU/battery usage for inactive tabs and background activity.
settings.rationale: This is a performance/battery-life recommendation rather than a security control; validate the exact Efficiency Mode level represented by this value against current Edge documentation if it needs to be reported precisely.

settings.id: Recommended - Scareware Blocker Blocks Detected Sites
settings.name: Recommended default: scareware blocker actively blocks detected sites
settings.description: Sets the recommended default for whether the scareware blocker actively blocks (rather than only warns about) detected fake virus-warning/tech-support scam pages.
settings.rationale: Recommending active blocking (rather than warn-only) provides stronger default protection against scareware while still allowing users to adjust the setting if needed.

settings.id: Recommended - Scareware Blocker Sends Detections to SmartScreen
settings.name: Recommended default: send scareware blocker detections to SmartScreen
settings.description: Sets the recommended default for sharing local scareware-blocker detections with Microsoft Defender SmartScreen.
settings.rationale: This mirrors the enforced 'Send Detected Sites to SmartScreen' control above, but as a user-overridable recommended default rather than a mandatory policy.

settings.name: Recommended default: enable Sleeping Tabs
settings.description: Sets the recommended default for enabling Sleeping Tabs, which frees up memory and CPU from inactive background tabs.
settings.rationale: This is a performance recommendation to improve responsiveness and battery life on managed devices with many open tabs.

settings.name: Recommended default: Sleeping Tabs timeout
settings.description: Sets the recommended default idle time before an inactive tab is put to sleep by the Sleeping Tabs feature.
settings.rationale: A 5-minute default balances memory/CPU savings against the inconvenience of tabs needing to reload when the user returns to them.

settings.id: WebView2 - New PDF Reader Applications List
settings.name: Applications using the new WebView2-based PDF reader
settings.description: Specifies which applications that embed the Edge WebView2 runtime should use the newer, WebView2-based PDF reader component.
settings.rationale: Standardizing all WebView2 host applications on the current, actively maintained PDF reader component keeps PDF rendering on the supported, patched code path.

changelog.notes: Release of Microsoft Edge for Business baseline version 1.0.0, converted from an Intune Settings Catalog export based on the Microsoft Edge SCT v151 reference template.
